Exchange halts withdrawals after $85M hot-wallet exploit

By Theo Marchetti

Oct 25, 2026

Mid-sized crypto exchange Orbitex suspended all withdrawals on Saturday after attackers drained about $85 million from one of its hot wallets, the company said in a statement.

The stolen funds were mostly ether and USDT, according to blockchain analytics firm ChainTrace, which traced roughly $52 million to addresses that began swapping the tokens for ether within an hour of the attack.

Orbitex said customer balances held in cold storage, which it put at more than 90% of total assets, were not affected. It said it would cover the losses from its own reserves and expected to reopen withdrawals within 72 hours.

The exchange's native token fell 23% in the hours after the announcement. Trading on the platform continued, but deposits of the affected tokens were paused.

It is the third exchange hack of more than $50 million this year. Investigators said early signs pointed to a compromised signing key rather than a flaw in the exchange's smart contracts.

Orbitex said it had notified law enforcement and was working with other exchanges to freeze the stolen funds. Tether said it had frozen about $9 million of the USDT involved.
